Thomson Reserve launch sales hit over 90% or 1,143 units at average of $2,900 psf
article:
Thomson Reserve , the first mega private residential development with over 1,000 units launched this year, saw 1,143 of its 1,268 units (90.1%) sold over the VIP preview on Oct 30 and launch day on Oct 31.

The units were sold at an average price of $2,900 psf, according to a joint statement by developers UOL Group and CapitaLand Development (CLD).

The sales make it the top-selling new condo launch of 2026 by number of units sold. It also marks the highest launch sales volume since ParkTown Residence in Tampines North sold 1,041 of its 1,193 units (87%) in February 2025.

Both developments are joint ventures between UOL Group, its subsidiary Singapore Land Group (SingLand), and CLD.

Sources said demand was strong across all unit types, particularly for larger apartments. All 350 three-bedroom and 174 four-bedroom units were sold, along with 26 of the 28 five-bedroom suites.

All 200 two-bedroom-plus-study units were also sold, leaving about 123 smaller two-bedroom units available. Together with the two remaining five-bedroom suites, only 125 units remain for sale at Thomson Reserve.

The four- and five-bedroom units were released during VIP bookings on Friday, Oct 30, and were almost entirely snapped up ahead of the official launch on Saturday.

The highest absolute price achieved was said to be $5.98 million ($3,306 psf) for a 1,808 sq ft five-bedroom suite on the 30th floor of the Luxury Collection, after a 6% + 2% discount.

Meanwhile, the highest psf price was $3,334 psf for a four-bedroom premium unit that fetched $4.56 million, also after a 6% + 2% discount.

Kelvin Fong, CEO of PropNex, attributes the strong take-up partly to the relatively affordable price quantum of the units.

“We believe buyers were likely drawn to the relatively affordable price quantum, with prices starting from $1.544 million for two-bedroom units and $2.503 million for three-bedroom units,” he says.

According to Mark Yip, CEO of Huttons Asia, 215 units were sold through multiple purchases, including those by families buying together and extended families seeking to live close to one another.

Huttons Data Analytics estimates that around 90% of buyers were owner-occupiers, with most residing in Districts 19 and 20. Buyers with private residential addresses accounted for an estimated 70%, while those with HDB addresses made up the remaining 30%.

The last mega condominium launch in the Thomson area was the 1,206-unit JadeScape in 2018, eight years before Thomson Reserve.

Marcus Chu, CEO of ERA Singapore, believes Thomson Reserve has tapped into pent-up demand from buyers seeking new homes in an established neighbourhood.

“Many are also buying the opportunity to remain in a familiar neighbourhood, close to their families, schools and the amenities they have grown accustomed to,” he says.

The strong sales followed a record turnout of 32,000 visitors over two weekends of public preview. Thomson Reserve also collected more than 3,300 cheques ahead of the launch, representing a subscription rate of over 2.6 times.

According to the developers, the majority of buyers were Singaporeans purchasing for their own stay and investment.

“The robust take-up reflects buyers’ confidence in Thomson Reserve’s distinctive proposition and strong product positioning,” says a spokesperson for the joint venture.

The developers attributed the project's appeal to its spacious, upscale homes, proximity to reputable schools and nature parks, and the popular Upper Thomson dining stretch.

The 99-year leasehold development is located at Bright Hill Drive, off Upper Thomson Road, with a sheltered walkway connecting it to Upper Thomson MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

“As the last major private residential launch scheduled for 2026, Thomson Reserve rounds off the year on a high note and provides a good sense of private housing demand heading into 2027,” says Fong.

“Buyers have moved quickly for projects in established neighbourhoods close to an MRT station that offer a broad choice of units at a manageable price quantum," adds Fong. "We expect new launches in 2027 that tick these boxes should find willing buyers.”

title: Smart Reads of the Week: DBS vs OCBC vs UOB, 6.5% REIT Yields, Retirement Income, and AI Stocks
article:
Singapore stocks have had a cautious week, with the STI slipping on Tuesday before stabilising on Wednesday as local bank shares recovered slightly. Meanwhile, volatile bond markets and inflation concerns continue to put pressure on Asian banks.
With markets unsettled, investors are asking two important questions: which stocks offer value today, and which can provide dependable income for the years ahead?
This week’s Smart Reads compares DBS, OCBC and UOB, examines Temasek-backed REITs offering yields of around 6.5%, and explores whether Venture Corporation can sustain its dividends.
We also look at how CPF LIFE and dividend stocks can work together to provide S$3,000 a month in retirement, alongside opportunities in SGX dividend stocks and Singapore Exchange shares.
Finally, we compare Nvidia with AMD and discuss whether selling your losing stocks during a market dip is always the right decision.
Here are this week’s top articles:
DBS, OCBC and UOB: Which Singapore Bank Stock Is the Best Buy Now?
Singapore’s three major banks offer different strengths. We compare which presents the most attractive opportunity today.
Want S$3,000 a Month in Retirement? Here’s How CPF LIFE and Dividend Stocks Can Work Together
Discover how CPF LIFE and dividend income can complement each other to support your retirement goals.
3 Temasek-Backed Blue-Chip S-REITs Offering 6.5% Distribution Yields
These established REITs offer attractive yields, but what should income investors consider before buying?
Is Venture Corporation’s Cash-Rich Dividend Payout Plan Sustainable?
Venture’s strong cash position supports its dividends, but can the company maintain its payouts over time?
3 SGX Dividend Stocks to Watch as the STI Dips
Market weakness could create opportunities for income investors seeking quality businesses at more attractive valuations.
Nvidia vs AMD: Which Chip Stock Is the Better Buy Today?
Two AI chip leaders offer different growth prospects. We compare their profitability, valuations and investment potential.
SGX Shares Have Been a Big Winner: Is It Still a Buy Today?
Singapore Exchange shares have enjoyed a strong run. We examine whether there is still room for further gains.
Should You Sell Your Losers When the Market Dips?
Selling a losing stock can feel sensible, but the right decision depends on more than its share price.
